title: Imagine If:
title_short: Tin Can · Alex · Everybody’s Good at Something
headline: A retired lawyer on a park bench says everybody is good at something, and that we have more in common than we think.
story: Alex sits on a Central Park bench with a tin can at his ear. He films people for fun: everybody’s good at something. He wants to record people before they are gone. He recorded his parents 40 years ago and has watched it dozens of times.
Then Kalindi asks if it is easy to find common ground. His answer: we have a lot more in common than people realize. One person, about 38 seconds.
do: Text on frame 1: “EVERYBODY’S GOOD AT SOMETHING.” Already on screen at 0:00.
Set the scene by 0:06: the two of them on the bench with the string, and the bench sign readable.
Crop left on Alex (navy shirt, sunglasses).
End on his common ground line.
Cut from the MXF. Match the look of the Tin Cans montage.
dont: Do not use 764_3903 4:36–7:50. Private family story (his and Kalindi’s). Never in any cut.
Stop the parents line at “dozens and dozens of times” (4:32.6).
No job title on screen. No place name.

tech: Picture: 764 MXF files, 16:9. The Monday brief says 1920×1080, 23.98 fps. Our probe could only read the proxies (960×540, 23.976 fps, several mono audio tracks). Check the MXF in the NLE before you set the timeline.
1080×1920 at 23.976 fps. Same as the source. No conversion.

A 9:16 crop of 1080p is 608 px wide, so it is already upscaled 1.78×. Keep punch-ins at 110% or less. Sharpen lightly. The talk is one wide shot. Alex is on the left third of the frame: crop left. People and bikes cross in front: use them to cover jump cuts.
Audio is in the camera. The MXF has several mono tracks. Solo each track and use the one with the clear voice. We did not measure the channels here.
−14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP peak. Any music 18–20 dB under the voice.
Royal-blue box #1E6FD6, white text, floating over the speaker. Max 2 lines. Keep the bottom 20% clear.
H.264 MP4, 1080×1920, about 16 Mbps. One file. 9:16 only. Deliver to Frame.io → Ready for Review.
checklist: Write “Search for Common Ground”: capital S, small “for”. Never SFCG, CGLA or a Preemptive Love logo on screen.
The hook text is already on screen at 0:00. It does not animate on. No logo, title card, name or fade at 0:00.
Captions match the audio word for word. Keep the speaker’s own grammar.
No camera-shutter sounds. Every jump cut is covered.
No animation in the middle (Kalindi: “it was inauthentic”).
No name and no place name on screen.
End card: Search for Common Ground lockup + sfcg.org. Nothing under it.
Cut from the MXF in RAW, never from the proxy. 9:16 only.
The string and the bench sign are on screen and readable by 0:15.
Nothing from 764_3903 4:36–7:50, sound or picture (the hug after 7:53 is fine).
Only Alex speaks, plus Kalindi’s one question.

decisions.b: The end card reads sfcg.org. Search is still building the Imagine If landing page (Yana owns it). One end-card pass across the batch when the link exists.
